newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ridley buys feed mill assets for US$65 mln.
newsitem.headline: Ridley buys feed mill assets for US$65 mln.

text.p: Ridley Corp said on Monday that it had reached agreement with Windy Hill Pet Food Co to acquire the feedmilling assets of Hubbard Milling Co for about US$65 million.

Ridley said the acquisition would almost double its North American stockfeed volumes to more than one million tonnes annually and would be operated by a U.S. unit of Ridley's Canadian-based Feed-Rite Ltd, to be renamed Ridley Canada Ltd.

It said Hubbard would give the company a strong presence in the Midwest market of the United States which was the major pig and dairy region of the country and offered excellent opportunities for long term sales growth.
Acquisition financing would be provided by The Bank of Nova Scotia, to be subsequently retired by a proposed equity financing by Ridley Canada, due for completion by end-June 1997.
Ridley said it would retain a majority interest in Ridley Canada, but did not provide further details.

Ridley managing director Gary Busenshut said the transaction should have a positive influence on the company's results in fiscal year 1998 and was expected to contribute to a slight reduction in the company's current gearing level.
The company reported a slight fall in 1996/97 first half net profit to A$10.94 million from A$11.95 million a year earlier.
In the 1995/96 (July-June) year, Ridley achieved a A$22.36 million net profit against A$21.43 million a year earlier.

Hubbard's stockfeed operations consisted of 14 facilities (11 feedmills and three molasses block plants) located in Minnesota, Iowa, Indiana, Ohio, Nebraska, California and North and South Dakota, the company said.

Ridley shares were steady at A$1.48 at 10.30 a.m. (0030 GMT) on Monday, valuing the company at A$333.71 million based on 225.77 million shares on issue. It has traded at a high of A$1.68 and a low of A$1.44 in the past 12 months.
